verdicts.evidence: rulesDir() guarantees the post-condition: the mission branch is only returned if existsSync(missionRules), otherwise the package's templates/rules — so the guard only fires if the installed package's templates/rules is MISSING, a mutilated node_modules, not an input ("files" in package.json ships templates/; the package's integrity is the axiom of the analysis, the mutant itself being a corruption of dist/; runward doctor turns this installation red independently, it reads templates/rules). Measured on every real input: zero difference (battery of 12 fixtures + fallback without rules/ → 6 architect rules). Sensitivity control, corrupted state rebuilt (templates without rules/ + mission without rules/): shipped → ordered red exit 1 ("only 0 ... floor is 6" ×5); mutated → exit 1 too, the audit replaced by "✗ ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir .../templates/rules" — same verdict, reachable through installation corruption only.

verdicts.evidence: The removed .sort() makes the order of expectedRules depend on the filesystem (readdir is not sorted by contract — ext4 returns it in hash order; compliance.readRules sorts explicitly "for the byte-identity invariant"). MEASURED locally with two architect rules named ﬀ-zz.md (U+FB00) and 😀-aa.md (non-BMP), not accounted for: APFS returns code-point order, .sort() UTF-16 order — shipped lists the violations "😀-aa" then "ﬀ-zz", mutated inverts them (same lines, inverted order, identical exit 1); and ARTIFACT surface: runward manifest --sync writes the scaffolded rows in expected's order — measured diff of the architecture.md files produced (the two rows swapped), so the bytes of a committed file now depend on the machine. On ext4 the divergence holds for ordinary ASCII names. Nothing sees it: each leg of the net runs on a single filesystem where the readdir order of the shipped corpora coincides with the sort, and none asserts the order.

verdicts.evidence: Without the .md filter, expectedRules reads EVERY entry of the rules/ directory. RECIPE 1: example mission, an operator backup contracts-governance.md.bak next to the rule (the corpus mechanism ignores it too, it only hashes .md files). MEASURED: shipped exit 0; mutated → the .bak carries a CRITICAL/architect frontmatter, the /\.md$/ strip does not apply, "✗ Architect · contracts-governance.md.bak — not accounted for...", exit 1 — an unrequirable slug appears in the verdict. RECIPE 2: a runward/rules/notes/ subdirectory → readFileSync(directory) throws EISDIR: shipped → full audit green exit 0; mutated → the whole audit replaced by "✗ EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read", exit 1. Nothing sees it: the shipped corpus and every fixture of the net contain only .md files, with no subdirectory or side file (find checked; an org corpus's migrations.json, without frontmatter, would stay invisible — it is the .bak and the subdirectory that diverge).

verdicts.evidence: endsWith("") is always true: the filter becomes a no-op, measured behaviour identical to removing the filter outright. Same recipes, re-measured under THIS mutant: contracts-governance.md.bak in rules/ → shipped exit 0, mutated "✗ Architect · contracts-governance.md.bak — not accounted for..." exit 1; subdirectory rules/notes/ → shipped audit green exit 0, mutated "✗ EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read" exit 1 (expectedRules does not have the try/catch that ruleSignatures has). The gate starts requiring manifest rows for files that are not rules, or collapses on a directory. Nothing sees it: shipped corpora and fixtures of the net 100 % flat .md (find checked).

verdicts.evidence: Without an anchor, replace removes the FIRST occurrence of ".md" instead of the extension: a name with an infix ".md" changes slug. RECIPE: example mission, rule a.mdx.md (HIGH, architect — a legal name an org corpus can carry), accounted for as n/a under its shipped slug "a.mdx" in architecture.md, lock re-signed. MEASURED: shipped → slug "a.mdx", row found, exit 0; mutated → slug "ax.md" (first .md removed from the middle of the name), "✗ Architect · ax.md — not accounted for in the Rule conformance manifest...", exit 1 — the gate requires a row under a name no file carries, incurable without renaming the rule. Nothing sees it: no shipped rule name and no fixture of the net contains ".md" anywhere other than as the extension.
